correctness.rationale: The algebra was reconstructed independently. For Pauli strings \(P_e=Z_iZ_jY_k\) and \(P_f\), each shared vertex at which one edge assigns \(Y\) and the other assigns \(Z\) contributes one anticommutation sign, so \(P_eP_f=(-1)^{m(e,f)}P_fP_e\). Both advertised star families have zero role mismatches for every edge pair, hence all rotations commute and every permutation gives exactly the same unitary. The chain generators \(A=Z_0Z_1Y_2\) and \(B=Z_1Z_2Y_3\) have one mismatch and anticommute. Exact expansion on \(|+\rangle^{\otimes4}\) gives overlap \(1-2\sin^2(a)\sin^2(b)\); at \(a=b=\pi/4\) the fidelity is \(1/4\). Independent symbolic role checks reproduced these conclusions.

originality.rationale: The primary RZZY hypergraph paper itself is the decisive comparison. It defines the generators \(Z_iZ_jY_k\), states that noncommuting edge operators support a one-to-one edge-ordered encoding, and explicitly advertises both star families. Direct inspection shows those displayed star generators commute pairwise, yet the paper does not formulate the resulting collapse of all edge orders or the general role-mismatch parity criterion. General Pauli-commutation/circuit-optimization literature is background rather than implication coverage of this source-specific injectivity correction.
residual_risks: The audit targets the cited first public version; a later correction or revision could alter the authors' claims, although no indexed second-version theorem covering this correction was located.
The commutation quotient is only a necessary identification: special weights, global phases, or state-dependent coincidences can create additional degeneracies.
